# When and how to report and pay GST

Your GST reporting cycle may be monthly, quarterly or annually, depending on your GST turnover and other requirements.

**Last updated** 14 September 2026

Print or Download

## On this page

- [When to report](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/when-and-how-to-report-and-pay-gst#ato-Whentoreport)
- [Changing your reporting cycle](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/when-and-how-to-report-and-pay-gst#ato-Changingyourreportingcycle)

## When to report

We issue your [business activity statement](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/preparing-lodging-and-paying/business-activity-statements-bas/goods-and-services-tax-gst/gst-reporting-methods) about 2 weeks before the end of your reporting period. The date for lodging and paying is shown on your activity statement.

Your GST reporting and payment cycle will be one of the following:

- [Monthly](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/when-and-how-to-report-and-pay-gst/monthly-gst-reporting) if your GST turnover is $20 million or more
- [Quarterly](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/when-and-how-to-report-and-pay-gst/quarterly-gst-reporting) if your GST turnover is less than $20 million and we have not told you that you must report monthly.
- [Annually](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/when-and-how-to-report-and-pay-gst/annual-gst-reporting) if you are voluntarily registered for GST. That is, you are registered for GST and your GST turnover is under $75,000 ($150,000 for not-for-profit bodies).

## Changing your reporting cycle

Depending on your circumstances, you can change the cycle you use to report and pay GST.  This may happen when your GST turnover changes or if you choose to report and pay using a different cycle.

If you elect to change your cycle early in the lodgment period (for example, in the first month of the quarter or at the beginning of the financial year) you can generally commence the new cycle straight away. Otherwise, the new cycle will take effect from the start of the next quarter or year.

[Contact us](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/contact-us) if you need to change your GST reporting and payment cycle.

[**Monthly GST reporting**](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/when-and-how-to-report-and-pay-gst/monthly-gst-reporting)

You must report and pay GST online each month if your business has a GST turnover of $20 million or more.

[**Quarterly GST reporting**](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/when-and-how-to-report-and-pay-gst/quarterly-gst-reporting)

GST reporting options if your business has a GST turnover of less than $20 million.

[**Annual GST reporting**](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/when-and-how-to-report-and-pay-gst/annual-gst-reporting)

If you are voluntarily registered for GST and have not made an election to pay GST by instalments, check your options.

[**GST instalments**](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/when-and-how-to-report-and-pay-gst/gst-instalments)

If you elect to pay GST by instalments, you pay quarterly then report your actual GST information annually.
